measured: call edge precision and recall against each language's type checker on six pinned checkouts

osnova.unreleased: C# object creation names the constructor it runs

machine: macOS, Darwin 25.6.0 on arm64 (Apple silicon), Node.js 26.10.0; times are wall clock on that machine

method.unit: call site: (caller file, 1-based line of the callee name, callee name)
method.oracle: For every call expression in the checkout the language's own type checker or compiler is asked for the callee's declarations. A site is in-repo when at least one declaration is inside the checkout, external when every declaration is outside it (standard library, packages, generated code), and undecided when the checker returns nothing.
method.trueEdge: the oracle resolved the site inside the checkout and the symbol span osnova names contains one of the oracle's declaration lines in the same file
method.falseEdge: the oracle decided the site and the symbol span osnova names contains none of the oracle's declarations, including an in-repo target where the checker says the callee is external
method.undecidedEdge: the oracle has no verdict for the site, or did not enumerate it; excluded from both rates
method.recall: distinct in-repo oracle sites covered by at least one true osnova edge / distinct in-repo oracle sites
method.python: every ast.Call callee identifier in every .py file, sent to pyright-langserver textDocument/definition (benchmarks/oracle/sites-python.py, truth-python.mjs)
method.typescript: every CallExpression and NewExpression in one ts.Program over every .ts and .tsx file, resolved with checker.getSymbolAtLocation and getAliasedSymbol (truth-typescript.mjs)
method.go: every ast.CallExpr whose callee is a name or a selector (generic instantiation stripped), resolved with types.Info.Uses after golang.org/x/tools/go/packages loads ./... with tests (truth-go/)
method.java: every MethodInvocationTree and NewClassTree, resolved with Trees.getElement after JavacTask.analyze (the constructor; the named type for an anonymous class), declaration line from the element's tree (TruthJava.java)
method.rust: every tree-sitter call_expression whose callee is a name, a path, a method field or a turbofish, sent to rust-analyzer textDocument/definition once the server is quiescent (sites-rust.mjs, truth-rust.mjs)
method.csharp: every InvocationExpressionSyntax and ObjectCreationExpressionSyntax with a named callee, bound with SemanticModel.GetSymbolInfo in compilations replayed from a real build's csc arguments with source-generator output (truth-csharp/)

limitations: The checker's own resolution is the reference; where it returns nothing the site is undecided and counts in neither rate. Dynamic dispatch the checker cannot see is invisible to both sides.

A checker names one declaration, the static one. Where a language has overloads (Java, C#), osnova keeps one symbol per qualified name and records which declaration a call binds only when the written argument count selects exactly one among the declarations of the resolved type, its written-partial parts and its declared base classes; an edge whose count fits several or none names the method but no declaration, is counted in overloadUndetermined and is not claimed. Rust cfg variants of one function still collapse to one record.

The unit key is (file, line, name). Two calls of the same name on one line share a verdict; falseEdgesWithCorrectTarget counts the false edges where osnova's target is the checker's declaration for the other call. Osnova records a call at the line of the callee name, the line the oracle uses; 0.11.0 recorded the first line of the call expression, which in a chain written one call per line could be lines above the name.
Line tolerance of one absorbs multi-line call formatting and could mask a wrong target declared on an adjacent line.

Each oracle sees one build configuration: cobra for darwin and windows, ripgrep for the host target with default features, gson on the classpath at JDK 27's language level, humanizer for net10.0 with .NET SDK 10.0.401 rather than the SDK 11 preview its global.json names. Code compiled only in other configurations is not enumerated.

Recall counts osnova call edges only; import, reference, extends and routes edges are not scored here. Claimed edges in files the oracle does not compile (other languages in the checkout, uncompiled projects) are undecided.
The ripgrep checkout carries an untracked .osnovaignore excluding HomebrewFormula/, a symlink to pkg/brew; it changes no Rust file.

A Java or C# call whose target has a single declaration that accepts the argument count keeps that declaration even when a base type of the class is outside the index (an external class, or a partial part that did not parse), although an unseen base overload may be the one the compiler binds. Withdrawing those edges cost 10 recall points on humanizer and 1 on gson for one fewer false edge (gson LinkedTreeMapTest.java:215), so they are kept and scored as claims.
